name: Grumman G-73 Mallard
summary: Twin-radial 10-seat amphibian built 1946–1951, the larger successor to the Goose and the first Grumman amphibian with tricycle gear; most survivors fly in the Bahamas and Pacific.

wings: Large, straight high wing with wingtip fuel tanks
engines: Two large radial (or turboprop) engines on the wing leading edge
fuselage: Big two-step hull with a long row of square windows
Tricycle landing gear with a nose wheel
tail: Large single fin and rudder with the horizontal tail on the aft hull

tellTales: Large twin-engine amphibian with a nose wheel
Long row of square windows along a deep hull
Tall single fin on an upswept aft hull

confusedWith.howToTell: The Goose is smaller with hull-mounted main wheels and no nose wheel; the Mallard has tricycle gear and wingtip tanks.
The Widgeon is a small five-seater with a stubby hull and a strut-braced tail; the Mallard is much larger.
The HU-16 Albatross is bigger still, with a gull-like wing, tall tail and military markings; the Mallard is a smaller civil amphibian.
